title: GitHub - matheuzgomes/gawain: Every Python type declared, every covenant kept.
excerpt: Every Python type declared, every covenant kept. Contribute to matheuzgomes/gawain development by creating an account on GitHub.
content_html:
gawain is a type annotation checker for Python. It requires annotations on variables, parameters, returns and class attributes, then runs a type checker, ty or pyrefly, to check that the types are correct.

Type checkers such as mypy, Pyright, ty and pyrefly infer the type of a variable that has no annotation. ruff's ANN rules and flake8-annotations ask for annotations on functions only. gawain also asks for them on variables and class attributes.

uv tool install "gawain[ty]"
gawain check src/

Warning

ty is in beta, and its diagnostics may change between versions. If that is a problem for your project, use pyrefly, or --no-types to run the annotation checks only.

Why

I built gawain only because I hate dict[str, Any] and wanted to do something about it. If your answer to this is "but Python already infers that" or "but my IDE infers it for me", then don't use it, little padawan.

What it reports

Given shop.py:

PORT = 8080
retries = 3
total = compute()


def send(to, body):
    print(f"to {to}: {body}")


class Order:
    def __init__(self, items: list[str]) -> None:
        self.items = items

gawain check shop.py prints:

[presence]
shop.py:1:1    GW001 variable 'PORT' has no type annotation
shop.py:3:1    GW001 variable 'total' has no type annotation
shop.py:6:5    GW003 function 'send' has no return type annotation
shop.py:6:10   GW002 parameter 'to' of function 'send' has no type annotation
shop.py:6:14   GW002 parameter 'body' of function 'send' has no type annotation
shop.py:12:14  GW004 attribute 'items' is not declared in the body of class 'Order'

6 errors (presence). Type check skipped until presence errors are fixed.

In the default mode, retries = 3 passes, because a literal has an obvious type. PORT is an UPPER_CASE name, so gawain treats it as a constant, and a constant needs Final. The literal still gives the type, so PORT: Final = 8080 passes.

When every annotation is in place, gawain runs the type checker on the same files and prints what it reports. The default checker is ty. Given prices.py:

def total(prices: list[int]) -> int:
    return "0"

gawain check prices.py prints:

[types]
prices.py:2:12  ty[invalid-return-type] Return type does not match returned value: expected `int`, found `Literal["0"]`

1 error (types).

Install

Install gawain with the extra of the type checker you want. ty is the default checker, and the ty extra pins it to 0.0.100:

uv tool install "gawain[ty]"
# or
pip install "gawain[ty]"

To use pyrefly instead, install the pyrefly extra, which pins pyrefly 1.4.1 and does not install ty:

uv tool install "gawain[pyrefly]"
# or
pip install "gawain[pyrefly]"

Then choose it with checker = "pyrefly" in [tool.gawain], or with --checker pyrefly. docs/configuration.md explains the switch.

pip install gawain without an extra installs only the gawain command. It then needs a checker on PATH, or --no-types to run the annotation checks only.

Usage

gawain check src/                  # annotations, then types
gawain check src/ --no-types       # annotations only
gawain check src/ --checker pyrefly  # pyrefly instead of ty
gawain check src/ --mode strict    # an annotation on every assignment
gawain check src/ --format json    # one JSON object, for tools

gawain exits with 0 when nothing is reported, 1 when it reports an error, and 2 on a usage error or when the type checker cannot run. The type checker's warnings are printed but do not fail the check.

Rules

Code Reports
GW001 A variable assigned with no annotation.
GW002 A parameter with no annotation.
GW003 A function with no return annotation.
GW004 A class attribute with no annotation, or a self.x that the class body does not declare.
GW010 A constant that is not annotated Final[T].
GW011 A bare Final, with no type.
GW020 Any in an annotation.

GW000 marks a file gawain cannot read, and GW900 and GW901 mark a broken or unused suppression. To silence a line, name the code:

value = load()  # gawain: ignore[GW001]

docs/rules.md has the full rules, the exemptions and the suppression syntax.

Modes

The default mode is obvious. A name may go without an annotation when its value has an obvious type and the name is never assigned again: a literal (count = 0), a container of literals (ids = [1, 2, 3]) or a constructor call (user = User("ada")). strict asks for an annotation on every assignment:

[tool.gawain]
mode = "strict"

docs/rules.md has the exact rules of each mode.

pre-commit

repos:
  - repo: https://github.com/matheuzgomes/gawain
    rev: v0.3.1
    hooks:
      - id: gawain

pre-commit installs the hook from this repository's source, so building it needs Rust 1.97 or newer. docs/configuration.md covers [tool.gawain], paths and the hook in detail.

Performance

On the CPython 3.14 standard library (1,847 files, 974,586 lines), median of 30 runs (5 for flake8-annotations):

Tool Checks Median
gawain, obvious mode variables, parameters, returns, attributes 0.46 s
gawain, strict mode variables, parameters, returns, attributes 0.36 s
ruff --select ANN parameters, returns 0.35 s
flake8-annotations parameters, returns 11.4 s

gawain ran with --no-types. This is one benchmark on one machine (AMD Ryzen 7 3700X, WSL2). docs/benchmarks.md has the versions and the commands to run it again.

Documentation

  • docs/rules.md: rules, modes, exemptions and suppression.
  • docs/configuration.md: paths, output, exit codes, [tool.gawain] and pre-commit.
  • docs/benchmarks.md: how the numbers above were measured.
  • Issues: bugs and ideas.

Acknowledgements

gawain reads Python with ruff_python_parser and checks types with ty, both by Astral, or with pyrefly, by Meta.

Name

I don't know, I just like the Arthurian tales. In Sir Gawain and the Green Knight, Gawain repeats the Green Knight's covenant word for word, keeps every bargain he makes and slips only once: he hides the green girdle. gawain asks the same of your code: every type declared, and every declared type kept. The mascot is the Green Knight's axe with that girdle.

License

MIT. See LICENSE.
